text:
maya: heads-up, I ran a microbenchmark across SM80 vs SM90 and Triton vs CUDA kernels to track the regression from PR #4213. results look noisy but there's a clear pattern where the fused-paged attention on SM80 wins short-seq p99, while flash2-fused on SM90 dominates long-seq throughput. kv cache behavior also differs - kv refills causing stalls on the triton variant. attaching notes.

ryan: can you paste the exact command you ran? want to reproduce locally.

maya: sure. command I used:
```bash
python perf/run_attention.py --model gpt-j --seq 512 --max-seq 2048 --kernel flash2,fused_paged --platform cuda --cuda 12.1,12.2 --sm 80,90 --batch 4,8 --kv-policy paged --warmup 200 --iters 1000
```
I ran permutations in CI matrix.

li: nice. what benchmarks (latency vs throughput)? numbers?

maya: summary (median across 5 runs):
- SM80 fused_paged, seq=512, batch=8: p50 12ms, p95 18ms, p99 28ms, tokens/s 1400
- SM90 flash2, seq=512, batch=8: p50 13ms, p95 22ms, p99 34ms, tokens/s 1300
- SM80 fused_paged, seq=2048, batch=4: p50 48ms, p95 72ms, p99 95ms, tokens/s 400
- SM90 flash2, seq=2048, batch=4: p50 36ms, p95 58ms, p99 82ms, tokens/s 520
Triton vs CUDA native (same SM90 hw):
- Triton flash2 (cuda 12.2): seq=2048: p99 regressed ~+18% compared to our cuda-kernel build; profiler shows extra memcpy spikes.

jen: oh interesting. memcpys usually point to staging buffers or fallback copy paths. did you capture NVTX or kernel timeline?

maya: yes, I added nvtx brackets around attention entry/exit. here's a slice of the CPU->GPU timeline from nsight (trimmed):
```
[ATTN_START] kernel: flash2_forward (cuda)  1.8ms
kernel: fused_paged_attn   2.1ms
memcpy H2D staging  0.9ms  <--- frequent on triton run
kv refill task        0.7ms  (serialized)
KV_CACHE_SWAP         0.5ms  (page-in)
[ATTN_END]
```
On Triton runs the staging memcpy appears between kv swap and kernel launch more often.

sam: @maya do you see this only with paged kv policy? what about full-kv in-memory?

maya: full-kv in-memory avoids the memcpy but uses ~9GB more memory. latency is cleaner but throughput drops slightly due to less batching density. paged is the one triggering the memcpy + stall pattern on Triton.

ryan: might be an allocator interaction — Triton runtime/driver may be choosing pinned vs pageable buffers differently. are we using pooled pinned allocator in the triton builds?

maya: Triton build uses their default allocator. our cuda-kernel binary uses our pooled pinned allocator (dev branch). difference shows up in profiler: triton has extra cudaMemcpyAsync paths.

ops-bot: deploy check: kernel-experiments/bench-1765432100 completed (ci/bench). artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/bench-1765432100/ (contains nvprof traces).

li: ok next steps: 1) reproduce minimal repro that forces memcpy, 2) test Triton but with our pooled allocator linked, 3) add NVTX around allocator calls. i can try (2) this afternoon.

jen: also check batching heuristic. I remember a change where we group by model+kernel only and not by seq length; that could create microbatches that interleave long and short sequences causing KV thrash.

maya: yep that's what I saw. when heuristic groups strictly by seq length bucket, p99 drops ~10-15% for paged policy. current default groups by model+priority.

sam: can we add a quick flag to force sequence-bucketed batching in perf runner? might be a good ablation.

maya: already added: --batch-bucket seq|model. I ran seq bucketed runs above.

ryan: curious about kernel selection logic: how are we picking flash2 vs fused_paged at runtime? any fallback that could trigger on SM capability bits?

maya: runtime chooses preferred kernel by (model arch, seq_len, sm capability, cuda version). there is a fallback table that maps to compat kernels; after PR #4213 we added an extra fallback to triton_flash2 when cuda>=12.2 which might be suboptimal for paged kv.

li: that fallback could be the culprit — it shifts to triton flash2 on newer cuda, which then hits the allocator/memcpy issue. if we revert fallback for paged-kv on sm90 it'll probably fix customer regressions.

jen: agree. but let's gather a short reproducible log and open a small PR to gate the fallback behind a knob. also add these perf numbers to the release notes.

maya: created issue: infra#1892 and linked perf artifacts. patch draft ready to gate fallback: patch uses env REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash2_cuda to test.

sam: i'll run the gated job on our dedicated pool (SM90 nodes) and try pooled allocator + triton. will report back.

infra-bot: Note: dedicated-sm90-pool has 12 slots free. Reserving 1 for sam for 2 hours.

ryan: thanks. one more ask — can someone run a small nsight timeline with memory tracker on both builds and attach side-by-side? that will help confirm memcpy origin.

maya: will do. attaching two trimmed timelines to s3 link in issue.

jen: excellent. if this ends up being allocator behavior we should consider normalizing allocator decisions across triton/native builds to avoid surprises.

li: and add a perf test in the PR that checks p99 regression for paged kv on long-seq. small guard.

maya: agreed. I'll open the PR after sam's run. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: quick update (later): ran pooled allocator + triton flash2 on sm90: memcpy spikes reduced, p99 improved from 82ms -> 68ms for seq=2048 (still slightly worse than native cuda-kernel at 62ms). looks promising.

ryan: great, looks like allocator parity mostly explains it. we should also check kernel launch overhead differences (Triton wrapping).

maya: noted. leaving this thread open until PR merges. logs/artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/bench-1765432100/ (nvtx, nsight, raw csv).

ops-bot: reminder: please add perf artifacts to the release-perf bucket if results used in changelog.

maya: done.
